page: Vultr voc-g-40c-160gb-768s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 40 dedicated vCPUs across 20 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. The instance is configured with 160.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, and is provisioned with 768 GB of local NVMe SSD storage along with a single complimentary public IPv4 address. It does not include dedicated graphics processing units.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing capability and high memory throughput. The server scores 123693.48 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 72888.75 in the Passmark CPU suite, placing its multi-threaded throughput in the top 25 percent. Large-block uncached memory benchmarks reach 451.84 GB/sec for reads and 262.45 GB/sec for writes, both ranking in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. In-memory data store performance is reflected by 84.31 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core execution metrics, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1827.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 29.39 GB/sec, fall within the middle 50 percent.

The qualitative balance of 40 dedicated AMD EPYC cores, robust memory bandwidth, and local NVMe storage makes this configuration cost-efficient for scale-out parallel workloads compared to memory-heavy or GPU-accelerated tiers. It presents a trade-off between moderate single-thread frequency and high multi-core aggregate throughput. Best-fit workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, Redis caching layers, medium-scale container orchestration clusters, batch data transformation pipelines, and parallel data analysis.

The server achieves strong multi-threaded results, scoring 123693.48 in stress-ng multi-core and maintaining uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 451.84 GB/sec, placing it in the top 10 percent for memory throughput.
